verdicts.strongest_argument: The finding's key negative assertion is falsified by its own document, and the positive facts are published company disclosure the market already repriced. The hunter writes that 'no sell-side note, consensus figure or preview exists anywhere in the capture to set a bar against'. But docs/2016f51865...txt line 52, dated 2026-06-04T00:40:58Z, publishes the whole Q1 release including the sentence 'Q2 sales are guided to $154M-$160M' - the company's own guided revenue range for the very quarter being reported on 2026-09-02. There is a bar, it is management's, and it is in the corpus. The same message publishes the $41.1m cash and no-debt datum, the 22.9% comp, the narrowed $8.0m net loss and the 28.9% gross margin, and line 48 relays the -0.26 EPS on $124.72m revenue. All of it is company disclosure from the 2026-06-03 print, which the market answered with +18.69% - the second-largest positive reaction in the seven-event record. So the balance sheet and the inflection narrative were published and priced in a measured move. What remains is weaker than it looks. The '$24m of projected net profit for the following year' is not an estimate: line 29 shows it is a single bullish StockTwits post of 2026-06-05 ('$24 mil projected net profit next year and they are turning positive next qt'), presented in the brief as 'the corpus's contemporaneous read'. Dressing a message-board number as a forecast is not evidence, and the arithmetic gives it away - $24m of net profit against a $117m market cap would be under 5x earnings, which is not a number the tape supports. And the residual claim, 'the quarter being reported here is the one the turnaround thesis is staked on', is true of every earnings print and carries no size. Finally the finding's structural argument - a five-week blackout in the capture means the decline 'carries no information' - is the inference I am explicitly instructed to reject in both directions: a thin capture is thin about everything, and asserting that a -32% slide from $5.60 to $3.81 is uninformative because the corpus stopped recording is reading a capture artefact as a fact about the market. I hold 15 points back because the corpus genuinely contains no third-party preview or estimate revision after 2026-07-24, so I cannot tell whether the market's markdown reflected a lowered bar for the $154-160m guide.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Publishes the full Q1 FY2026 release - 22.9% comps, $124.7m sales, net loss narrowed to $8.0m, 28.9% gross margin, $41.1m cash with no debt - and, critically, 'Q2 sales are guided to $154M-$160M', i.e. company guidance for the quarter this print reports.
The turnaround/margin-inflection thesis the finding rests on was published as a standalone analysis on 2026-06-09 and relayed in the captured feed.
The last company disclosure before the print is a public 8-K on a material agreement; the August 13 filing is a passive 13G.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The Q1 disclosure - cash, no debt, comps, and the $154-160m Q2 guide - was priced in a measured event: 2026-06-03 amc, +18.69%, against a 12.31% seven-event median. Since then the market has repriced the name hard: spot 3.81, -30.09% from the 52-week high, run_up_20d -8.85%, on a 339,310-share average volume. The finding treats that decline as informationless; nothing in the bars supports that reading, and I will not accept a drawdown as evidence a bullish thesis is unpriced any more than I would accept a run-up as evidence a bearish one is. Baseline is sound (fits_cadence, 7 events) though it carries one session_conflict on the 2025-12-03 event, which widens the true reaction distribution rather than narrowing it.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated third-party estimate for the July quarter sitting materially below the company's own $154-160m guide, or above it - i.e. an actual bar to compare the guide against - rather than a five-week gap in the capture treated as a market blind spot.

interactions: The claim and its 'independence' corroboration both reduce to the same two artefacts: one StockTwits document and the filings.json index. The independence note's substance - that the run-in contains no company news - is a statement about the absence of filings, which is verifiable, but the inference that therefore the price decline is uninformative is not.
corpus_limits: TLYS's capture holds 45 items, three stored bodies and no news documents, with nothing at all between 2026-07-24 and the print. That gap is a property of the capture's query set and schedule; I have not read it as evidence either that the market was uninformed or that it was informed. There is no sell-side note, no analyst preview and no independent consensus figure to compare with the company's $154-160m Q2 guide. No options chain, so no implied move or skew.
